purpose: TavrWorkbench helps reviewers inspect, rate, and correct TAVR CT segmentations and anatomical measurements case by case. It also regenerates annular measurements and produces a parametric valve model for export.
summary: The source has concrete data-loss paths: a crafted case ID can escape the output folder, the dataset packager can recursively delete unrelated files, and the macOS installer may delete an existing Slicer installation after a startup failure. The catalog build also omits the Python helper package required to load the module. 🔴 Do not merge yet: fix the data-loss paths and verify the selected catalog revision and packaged build.

safety.rationale: Inspected case ID handling and output writes, dataset cleanup, and the standalone installers. They contain concrete paths to unintended overwrites or deletion; the installed module's networking and the separate download installers were also reviewed.

environment.rationale: The module disables VTK warnings globally at import in TavrWorkbench.py. The requirements file is empty and the repository search did not reveal runtime pip installation.

packaging.rationale: TavrWorkbench/CMakeLists.txt lists only the main Python script, whereas that script imports the omitted TavrWorkbenchLib package. Root CMake declares no extension dependencies, matching the supplied entry, but I could not build or independently resolve its revision.

license.rationale: LICENSE.md grants noncommercial redistribution of unadapted material, but prohibits sharing adaptations and commercial use. The original scripts described as sources of the annulus pipeline and external sample data terms were not independently checked.

soundness.rationale: Inspected case navigation, segmentation and measurement lifecycle, storage, and the geometry test. Navigation does not check unsaved segmentation edits, and a failed volume load is nevertheless marked as a loaded case.

utility.rationale: README.md provides a manifest example and workflow, and the main module contains a geometry test. Some documented input and review options differ from the current code, and the registered sample datasets are explicitly placeholders.

findings.title: Dataset packaging can delete files outside the case directory
findings.explanation: safe_name permits the case ID '..', and package constructs case_rel as cases/<ID>. For such a manifest, cleanup walks cases/.., i.e. the whole selected output directory, and removes files not in the new entry, including unrelated data. Even normal IDs cause untracked files in an existing case folder to be deleted without confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Reject dot components, verify resolved paths remain beneath a dedicated case directory, and remove only files recorded as generated by a previous run, with explicit confirmation or a non-destructive default.

findings.title: Case IDs can escape the output folder or collide
findings.explanation: A manifest case_id of '..' remains '..'; case_dir joins it to the selected output root, so saving a review or mask writes into its parent and can overwrite existing review.json or segmentation.seg.nrrd. Distinct IDs such as 'a/b' and 'ab' also map to the same folder, so one case can overwrite another case's corrections while their status entries remain distinct.
findings.suggestion: Reject '.' and '..', enforce resolved-path containment, and use a collision-resistant mapping or reject duplicate normalized case IDs before loading.

findings.title: macOS installer can delete an existing Slicer installation after a failed start
findings.evidence:
local broken="$SLICER_APP"
        rm -f "$MARKER"
        install_slicer fresh
        if [ "$SLICER_APP" = "$broken" ]; then
            # The standard location holds the broken copy itself: replace it with a fresh download
            rm -rf "$broken" 2>/dev/null || true
            [ ! -e "$broken" ] || die "Slicer at $broken cannot start. Drag it to the Trash, then run the command again."
            install_slicer fresh
findings.explanation: The installer may reuse an existing same-version Slicer application, not necessarily one it installed. If macOS terminates that process during configuration, the recovery path can recursively delete that application without asking, including any user modifications stored in it; a process termination does not prove the application is disposable.
findings.suggestion: Never automatically remove an existing Slicer application; install a separate copy or request explicit confirmation after identifying its ownership and backing it up.

findings.title: Packaged module omits its required helper package
findings.explanation: TavrWorkbench.py imports TavrWorkbenchLib.cases and other helpers at module import, but no helper files are listed for installation in this CMake file. A catalog-built package therefore lacks the package and cannot import the module, even though running from the source tree can work. This is a non-blocking extension packaging defect under the index admission policy.
findings.suggestion: Install all TavrWorkbenchLib Python files with their package directory preserved, and test loading the installed package in a clean Slicer.

findings.title: Import disables VTK warnings for the entire Slicer process
findings.evidence:
# Suppress VTK warnings globally to prevent console flooding and UI freezing
vtk.vtkObject.GlobalWarningDisplayOff()
findings.explanation: Once the module imports, VTK warnings from Slicer and other extensions are suppressed globally, including for users who never open TavrWorkbench. This hides diagnostic information unrelated to this module.
findings.suggestion: Remove the global toggle or narrowly handle the specific warnings in the operation that causes them.

findings.title: Navigating away discards unsaved mask edits without warning
findings.explanation: The leave check covers hinge and measurement edits but not segmentation edits. When a reviewer paints a mask and navigates without clicking Save Mask, loading the next case removes the current segmentation node, losing the changes without a prompt.
findings.suggestion: Track segmentation modifications and prompt to save, discard, or cancel navigation.

findings.title: A failed image load is still marked as a loaded case
findings.evidence:
self._cacheReview()      # keep in memory so Prev/Next doesn't lose ratings
        self.current_index = idx
        self._loadCaseData()
        self._case_loaded = True
        self._restoreReview(idx)
findings.explanation: _loadCaseData returns False when the image cannot be loaded, but this caller ignores the result and sets _case_loaded to True. The interface can then show the failed case as loaded and permit review actions despite the missing volume.
findings.suggestion: Check the return value and leave the case unloaded, with review actions disabled, on failure.

findings.title: License limits redistribution and commercial use
findings.evidence:
the Licensed Rights in the Licensed Material to:
             A. reproduce and Share the Licensed Material, in whole or in part,
                for NonCommercial purposes only; and
             B. produce and reproduce, but not Share, Adapted Material for
                NonCommercial purposes only.
findings.explanation: The license permits noncommercial sharing of the unadapted material, but users cannot rely on it for commercial use or to distribute adaptations. This is a material restriction for prospective users, not by itself evidence that an unmodified catalog package cannot be distributed.
findings.suggestion: Make the restrictions prominent in extension metadata and documentation, and retain required attribution in distributed packages.

findings.title: Documentation describes workflows absent from the current module
findings.evidence:
The Input panel offers two ways to load a dataset. Choose one using the Directory or JSON Manifest option.

### Directory Mode

Select a folder that contains your volumes in .nii, .nii.gz or .nrrd format. The module finds the cases in one of three ways.

1. Automatic pairing: each volume is matched with a mask that shares its name and ends with _mask, for example case01.nii.gz and case01_mask.nii.gz.
findings.explanation: The inspected module sets up a JSON map selector and calls read_data_map; it does not implement the documented directory input. The README also describes a three-option rating scheme while the current interface uses Approve and Flag, which can mislead new reviewers.
findings.suggestion: Update the tutorial and output descriptions to match the current UI, and provide a representative sample manifest and clinical-use limitations.
